summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, diastolic heart failure, and a history of mitral valve repair was admitted for hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state and back pain following multiple falls. She was treated in the MICU with an insulin drip, which was transitioned to increased NPH insulin. Fluid overload was managed with IV furosemide and metolazone, reducing her weight from 93 kg to 77 kg. A urinary tract infection initially caused by E. coli was treated with ceftriaxone, but she later developed a resistant Pseudomonas infection, managed with fosfomycin after catheter removal. She also developed C. difficile colitis, treated with vancomycin. Her anemia was addressed with a blood transfusion and iron supplementation. She was discharged to an extended care facility on torsemide, insulin, vancomycin, and fosfomycin, with plans for follow-up on wound care, infection resolution, and evaluation of an incidental abdominal wall finding.
problems: Diabetes with hyperosmolarity, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Pseudomonas infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
